papers.title: CONCEPTUAL EMERGENCE & GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 06 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · October 2026 ABSTRACT When do interactions among concepts, models, tools and people produce a genuinely new, independently verifiable capacity rather than a novel label or a misleading evaluation threshold? This English-language research monograph develops a falsifiable program for conceptual emergence and generative intelligence. Its research three-coupling is Interaction Generation × New-Function Identification × Counterfactual Verification. The proposed emergence expression compares held-out capability improvement with the strongest viable baseline and a contamination penalty, with all terms requiring operational definition and appropriate normalization before use. RESEARCH DESIGN The volume studies both smooth scaling and possible discontinuities, evaluation-metric sensitivity, training-data leakage, compositional generalization, simple-rule baselines, factorial component ablation, multi-agent collaboration, correlated errors, human-AI complementarity, multimodal grounding, causal interventions, tool-dependence, calibration, cross-model reproducibility, governance, and intergenerational handoff. A claimed capability must survive preregistered unseen tasks, strong comparators, counterfactual perturbations and independent reproduction. A fluent explanation, a generated new term or a model's assertion of consciousness is not evidence of functional emergence. MONOGRAPH STRUCTURE The 82 research chapters each present one distinct proposed chapter-wide operational equation, followed by twelve independently paginated study sections. Thirty advanced physics derivation routes appear in the preface with three-dimensional conceptual diagrams; they are existing physics statements within specified domains and do not establish laws of language or awareness. The concluding 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos each feature one of 233 distinct physical equation anchors. These equations are methodological contrasts and educational prompts, not proof of the emergence hypotheses. A separate Excel workbook indexes chapters, sections, gates, candidate mechanisms and physics anchors. EVIDENCE AND ETHICS This monograph is a theoretical and experimental research agenda. It reports no new trials, controlled effects or validated discoveries; all proposed mechanisms, metrics, forecasts and outcomes are UNVERIFIED until independently tested. The distinction between appearance under a chosen test and a robust new function must be maintained. Consent, intellectual provenance, lawful data use, security and affected persons' right to refuse are hard constraints rather than offsettable penalties. OPEN RESEARCH INVITATION Research Gates reserve space for questions that can be rejected, refined or answered by future researchers. Phoenix Answer Embryos are provisional designs that can be falsified, decomposed, recombined or responsibly retired. The goal is not a permanent claim that machines awaken or that thought obeys physical equations; it is an enduring, contestable toolkit for recognizing and scrutinizing useful new functions. FOUNDATIONS Project source: Living Concept Civilization — Eighteen Tri-Coupled Flagship Research Programs, v2.0 (2026-10-13), Flagship 06. Wei et al., Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models (2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07682. Schaeffer et al., Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage? (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.15004. Chollet, On the Measure of Intelligence (2019), https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01547. Wilkinson et al., FAIR Guiding Principles (2016), https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18.

papers.title: An evaluation guided multiagent framework for generating floor plans that comply with municipal building regulations
papers.summary: Abstract Generative models often produce perceptually plausible outputs that violate hard domain rules. In architectural layout generation, balancing geometric intuition with regulatory compliance remains a persistent challenge, as current frameworks routinely fail to conform to local building laws. This paper proposes LayoutGen, a multi-agent neuro-symbolic framework coupling probabilistic generation with deterministic verification in an evaluation-guided refinement loop. LayoutGen employs a four-phase retrieval-driven pipeline (spatial reasoning, coordinate mapping, vector rendering, and iterative refinement) powered by a dual retrieval engine leveraging architectural precedents and legislative laws. An Evaluation Engine scores the generated 2D Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) layouts and returns a graded, itemised report. Every scored quantity is computed by deterministic geometric checks over the generated coordinates against a structured rule repository; the Large Language Model (LLM) is confined to spatial planning, coordinate proposal, and the natural language feedback that drives refinement, together with an advisory Vaastu commentary that does not enter the grade. papers.title: A Survey-Informed Vision of Open-Source Agents: From Rights to Handoffable Maintenance
papers.summary: Open source gives recipients rights to use, study, modify, and redistribute software, but language-model agents distribute behavior across code, learned parameters, prompts, tools, retrieval, configuration, and runtime state. These mechanisms complicate maintenance in open and proprietary systems alike. Public delivery adds a distinct question: whether recipients obtain enough rights, materials, checks, and modification entry points to exercise maintenance capability and pass it onward. We call this objective handoffable maintenance: a verified maintenance result produced by one recipient becomes a practical starting point from which a subsequent recipient can complete a predefined bounded change. This survey-informed vision separates release-side readiness from demonstrated handoff and organizes prior work through eight maintenance-operation families, artifact roles, preservation relations, evidence, and recipient conditions. It identifies four research pathways: independently usable modification sources; public repair resources derived from restricted failures; propagation of public repairs through customized forks; and recipient-side replacement of propagated unreliable contributions. Each pathway specifies its deliverable, preservation requirements, strong comparisons, and falsifiable prediction. A shared evaluation design distinguishes a full-support reference, independent

papers.title: Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Memory Management, Coordination Failures and Semantic Conflict Resolution
papers.summary: As large language model (LLM) systems move from using one agent at a time to working with multiple agents together, keeping the system stable and ensuring memory stays accurate is still a major challenge. Making linear tasks work with multiple agents hurts performance by up to 70% because of extra communication and problems that spread out, but tasks that can be done at the same time can improve performance by up to 81% (Kim et al., 2025). Right now, the memory management tools we use like flat conversation logs, RAG retrieval and single-agent versioning systems (Wu et al., 2025; Su et al., 2026) do not work well when there are conflicts in open-domain semantic merges. They either need strict locks or special compilers for specific domains to handle these issues. To tackle these bottlenecks, this review paper brings together real-world failure categories, system-level checks and memory designs. It introduces a Git-managed multi-agent framework that includes dynamic task assignment, secure branch execution in isolated environments and external oversight using an LLM as a judge, along with council-based meaning-based decision making. In the end, we identify and outline the main research questions that still need to be addressed in areas like sharing experiences between different agents, figuring out the causes of faults and resolving conflicts in meaning.

papers.title: LLM Agents for Automated Post-Training via Structured Recipe Optimization
papers.summary: Automated post-training transforms pre-trained large language models (LLMs) into models capable of handling diverse domains by automatically constructing and optimizing a recipe of coupled decisions over data sources, data processing, cross-domain composition, and training configuration under a limited experimental budget. Existing automation either searches predefined recipe spaces that enable systematic optimization but remain fixed rather than adapting their available choices to the target tasks, or uses open-ended agents that discover task-specific choices but leave them implicit in trial-level edits, limiting their systematic reuse and recombination across trials. To fill this gap, we introduce optimization over a task-adapted recipe space, a novel paradigm that can adapt the recipe space itself to the target tasks while representing its choices explicitly for systematic reuse, recombination, and joint optimization. We instantiate this paradigm with Structured Recipe Optimization (SRO), comprising an LLM-based Recipe-Space Designer that constructs the task-adapted recipe space and a Multi-Domain Recipe Optimizer that uses structured trial evidence to guide LLM candidate construction and multi-objective Bayesian trial selection. Extensive experiments show that SRO achieves the highest average score in all evaluated target-model and agent-LLM combinations. In joint post-trai

papers.title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence. We organize the analysis around major system challenges, including computation, distributed execution and system software, resource management and serving, security and privacy, data management, and standardization. We further examine representative resource‐management strategies and emerging paradigms, including serverless inference, federated and decentralized learning, trustworthy distributed AI, and heterogeneous computing with emerging accelerators. papers.title: Reproducible research by design: design principles for low-code/no-code AutoML tools
papers.summary: Reproducibility is a major challenge for responsible machine learning (ML) research, especially with low-code/no-code automated ML (LCNC AutoML) tools making ML methods accessible to researchers outside data science. Existing approaches to support research reproducibility are difficult to apply to LCNC AutoML due to a lack of shareable code, limited tool transparency, and varying levels of ML expertise among users. To inform the design of LCNC AutoML tools that support reproducible research, this design science study proposes a set of design principles utilizing the theoretical lens of Technology Affordances and Constraints Theory. We first identified design requirements based on user studies with six researchers who implemented and reproduced LCNC AutoML projects. This was followed by a technical review of eight LCNC AutoML tools to identify existing design features in relation to the identified design requirements. Through mapping design features to design requirements, a set of design principles emerged: (1) GUI Customizability, (2) Standardized Reporting, (3) Interoperability, and (4) Adaptive Guidance. Together, these principles provide actionable design guidance for developing LCNC AutoML tools that support the documentation and reproducibility of ML research.

papers.title: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
papers.summary: The rise of autonomous AI agents represents a major paradigm shift in how users interact with mobile devices. Frameworks such as MobileRun and Mobile-Use can autonomously navigate Android applications and execute complex multi-step tasks. To interpret user interfaces, these frameworks rely primarily on Android accessibility (A11y) trees and secondarily on visual screenshots. In this paper, we demonstrate that this architectural dependence on unsanitized accessibility metadata, together with visual input, introduces a systemic vulnerability to indirect prompt injection. We show that adversarial prompts can cause autonomous agents to abandon their original objectives, violate context boundaries, and perform unauthorized device actions. Our empirical evaluation demonstrates goal hijacking, context drift, and unauthorized actions across visually hidden and fully exposed attack scenarios. In aggregate, MobileRun reaches an attack success rate of 0.822 with Gemma4:31B, while Mobile-Use with Qwen3.6:35B reduces this to 0.150 but does not eliminate context drift or unauthorized actions. These findings reveal that current mobile agent frameworks fail to enforce semantic context boundaries, treating passive environmental text as trusted instructions. Finally, we present a taxonomy of these attacks and discuss the need for zero-trust input validation, dedicated security agents, and strict

papers.title: Fragmented control, collective risk: multi‐agent AI and the coming governance crisis
papers.summary: Abstract Multi‐agent artificial intelligence (MAAI) systems are increasingly deployed across economic and digital infrastructures. Existing regulatory frameworks, including the EU AI Act and related initiatives, largely focus on individual AI systems and are therefore poorly suited to govern risks that arise from agent interaction. This paper argues that multi‐agent AI introduces distinct governance challenges, including emergent behavior, tacit coordination, cascading systemic risks, and difficulties in assigning accountability. Traditional risk management approaches, which rely on static and component‐based analysis, are inadequate for adaptive, networked systems operating across jurisdictions. Through a comparative review of policy developments in the European Union, United States, and Asia‐Pacific region, the paper identifies a growing governance gap, alongside early regulatory experimentation such as China's emerging standards for intelligent agents. The paper concludes that effective oversight will require a shift from model‐centric regulation toward system‐level and adaptive governance frameworks capable of addressing the collective dynamics of multi‐agent AI systems.

papers.title: Agentic Displacement in Second Language Writing: The Acquisitional Consequences of Delegating Writing to Autonomous AI Browsers
papers.summary: Autonomous AI browsers such as Perplexity Comet and Copilot Mode in Microsoft Edge can receive a writing assignment, draft a response, and submit it with little language produced by the learner. To explain what this means for second language (L2) writing, this conceptual paper introduces the term agentic displacement. Full delegation transfers planning, writing, and revision to the agent, removing opportunities for the learner to produce language and regulate the writing process. The paper argues that this loss may limit language development. Delegation is a continuum; the paper traces its extreme, full replacement, through production-based accounts of acquisition. No empirical data are reported; the paper offers a framework, five testable propositions, and three dimensions of teacher practice: recognizing displacement, auditing tasks for delegability, and using pedagogical judgment to recover the learning a task was meant to produce. The central risk is developmental, not only ethical or procedural.

papers.title: The Reflection Penalty: when managers accept leadership coaching from a human but not an AI agent
papers.summary: Leadership coaching develops managers but is expensive and difficult to scale. AI may be able to help scale access, but “answering machine” like AI coaching agents invite cognitive offloading and weaken learning. We instantiated a human coaching protocol, supported across prior cycles, as a text-based AI coach built to prompt reflective questioning. In the fourth cycle of a design-based research program at a global consulting firm, eight managers received the same protocol from a human coach and the AI coach, applied each session in an observed onboarding activity, and reflected on both in interviews. All eight welcomed the probing questions and preferred the human coach. Notably, they resisted the same protocol of questioning from the AI coach and wanted answers from it instead. This study’s theoretical contribution is the Reflection Penalty, the cost an AI coach pays for asking a user to do the reflective work that makes human coaching effective. Its practical contribution is a jobs-to-be-done map for AI coaching, assembled from proposals participants raised on their own. It divides coaching into distinct jobs and assigns each to the human or the AI best suited to it. Both contributions are offered to those designing AI tools that aim to support reflection

papers.title: Agency and Embodiment Provide Dissociable Benefits to Perception, Metacognition and Neural Processing During Active Sensing
papers.summary: Metacognition, judging how reliable our own perceptual decisions are, is central to adaptive behavior. Such judgments hinge on the reliability of the sensory evidence on which that decision is based, and active sensing through self-directed exploration is known to improve perception itself. Yet, how agency, the authorship over self-initiated actions, and the processing of the sensory consequences, which is implicit to active sensing, modulate metacognition and its calibration, remains unknown. Whether physical embodiment adds to this beyond virtual exploration is similarly unclear, yet relevant both for daily life and for self-monitoring in agentic AI. Here, we combined a naturalistic auditory search paradigm with mobile electroencephalography. Twenty participants performed a target-detection task under three conditions: active embodied exploration , active screen-based exploration, and passive listening to replays of their own trials, while we obtained steady-state auditory evoked potentials (SSAEPs) to characterize stimulus-locked neural responses. We find that both agency conditions improved accuracy, metacognitive sensitivity, and overall SSAEP amplitude relative to passive listening, indicating that agency, rather than whole-body movement, drives these enhancements. papers.title: Multi-modal meta-analysis of functional genomics data to identify regulatory relationships in the brain
papers.summary: Assigning target genes to a transcription factor (TF) is a persistent challenge in gene regulatory biology. No single assay directly observes a regulatory relationship, and the commonly used individual data types, perturbation-response transcriptomics, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-seq) binding, and gene co-expression, each carry substantial sources of noise and bias when used alone. In this thesis, I present an integrative computational pipeline that aggregates all three modalities into a single, transparent per-gene ranking for a queried TF, converting each modality's evidence to a common Z-score scale via empirical tail probabilities and combining them with Stouffer's weighted Z-score method. I applied the pipeline across 188 TFs and assessed its validity across these TFs. I assessed empirical validity from several independent angles: volume-matched null models, cross-modality concordance testing, comparison against an internally curated database of experimentally supported TF-target relationships, and an agentic PubMed/Europe PMC literature-screening pathway. The modality-swap null models showed that each individual modality carried substantial TF-specific information, and cross-modality concordance across the full candidate pool was significantly positive for all three modality pairs. Curated-database recovery, by contrast, was sparse and strongly bimodal across TFs,

papers.title: A longitudinal evaluation of a university-wide faculty development grant program: pedagogical innovation, student priorities, and programmatic evolution
papers.summary: Background Faculty development grant programs are strategic levers for improving teaching quality, curriculum design, and student learning, yet longitudinal evaluations remain scarce. In this study, we assess King Saud University's Program for Excellence in Learning and Teaching (PELT)— an early university-wide faculty teaching-grant initiative —examining its implementation, faculty uptake, and programmatic evolution over a decade. Methods Using a longitudinal, multi-source program-evaluation design, we analyzed eight PELT cycles through 157 completed grants, faculty ( n = 108) and student ( n = 413) surveys, and descriptive benchmarking against 11 international peers. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and selected faculty ratings were compared using Mann–Whitney U -tests. Results PELT evolved from a high-volume inaugural phase (71 grants) to a more selective model (6–11 grants annually) with a 95.7% completion rate. Participation remained broadly balanced across Humanities (34.4%), Science (30.6%), and Health (28.0%), supporting cross-disciplinary engagement. Teaching and assessment strategies (51% of funded projects) consistently dominated, with targeted emphases on job-market skills and e-learning in specific cycles. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs' data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs' training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs' data properties. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs' data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.

papers.title: The need for uncertainty: why probabilistic LSTMs are key to improving flood predictions and enabling learned warning rules
papers.summary: Abstract. Deterministic model predictions can struggle to adequately capture extreme events such as floods and droughts, which are of particular relevance in hydrology. This limitation arises because deterministic models collapse the conditional runoff distribution to a single point estimate. Probabilistic modeling provides a way to address this issue by explicitly representing uncertainty and assigning non-zero probabilities to a range of possible outcomes, including rare and extreme events, thereby capturing the full range of plausible hydrological responses. Motivated by this perspective, we examine whether probabilistic Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models improve the representation of extreme events in rainfall–-runoff simulations across Switzerland. Overall, the probabilistic models show good calibration, although some miscalibration remains for the extremes. Differences between models mainly manifest in how uncertainty is distributed: some approaches produce narrower and lighter-tailed distributions, while others yield broader distributions with heavier tails. These trade-offs highlight that probabilistic models differ not only in sharpness but also in how their calibration for rare events. We observe this tradeoff also in models' accuracy metrics. papers.title: AI-driven whole-life costing for decision-ready UK public building retrofits
papers.summary: Abstract Public-sector building retrofits in the United Kingdom require decisions that balance whole-life cost, carbon reduction, service continuity and auditability under limited data and constrained capital budgets. This paper develops a decision-ready whole-life costing (WLC) workflow that integrates environmental, social and governance (ESG) priorities with uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence (AI) for public-building retrofit appraisal. The workflow combines national non-domestic Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) and Display Energy Certificate (DEC) data, Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme (PSDS) delivery evidence and stakeholder inputs to construct a scenario library of public-building archetypes, retrofit actions and appraisal constraints. Stakeholder priorities from interviews, a questionnaire and a co-design workshop are translated into transparent weights using fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (F-AHP). These weights parameterise a reinforcement learning (RL) planner, while a Bayesian convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (BCNN–LSTM) surrogate provides uncertainty-bounded energy, carbon and cost trajectories for repeated policy evaluation. papers.title: Perceived Readiness for Artificial Intelligence Enabled Auditing in Power Equipment Procurement at Guangxi Electric Power Vocational and Technical College
papers.summary: The research objectives were 1) to explore stakeholders’ perceptions of the key enabling conditions associated with the applicability of AI-enabled auditing in power equipment procurement, and 2) to explore experts’ perspectives on the applicability and expected governance contributions of AI-enabled auditing in power equipment procurement. The sample consisted of 255 respondents involved in equipment procurement, auditing, management, and utilization at Guangxi Electric Power Vocational and Technical College and three experts who participated in the focus group discussion. The instruments used were a structured questionnaire and a semi-structured focus group discussion guide. The quantitative data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, and standard deviation, and the qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings revealed that 1) stakeholders perceived the five key enabling conditions at an overall high level (M = 3.70, S.D. = 0.77); Data Quality received the highest evaluation, while Auditor Competency received the lowest evaluation and was at a moderate level, indicating a particular need for AI-related professional development, and 2) the experts perceived AI-enabled auditing as applicable to transaction analysis, supplier evaluation, document review, risk identification, compliance monitoring, audit-efficiency improvement, education cost cont

papers.title: PROCEEDINGS BOOK OF THE XXXII SYMPOSIUM “BIOINFORMATICS AND COMPUTER-AIDED DRUG DISCOVERY”
papers.summary: The materials of the XXXII International Symposium Bioinformatics and Computer-Aided Drug Discovery (Virtual, October 19–21, 2026) are presented. The Symposium is dedicated to addressing the emerging challenges and opportunities in in silicodrug discovery. It covers contemporary areas of biomedical science focused on analyzing normal and pathological states of the organism and elucidating pathological processes at the cellular and molecular levels. The main topics include the development and practical application of computational methods for identifying and validating new pharmacological targets, in silico design of potent and safe pharmaceutical agents, optimization of the structure and properties of drug-like compounds, and rational approaches to the use of pharmacotherapeutic agents in medical practice. This information will be valuable to researchers developing computational methods and applying them to drug research and development using bioinformatics and chemoinformatics approaches based on post-genomic technologies. It may also be of interest to undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate students specializing in related fields.

papers.title: Transformer-based Digital Biomarker Identification for Early Neurological Assessment
papers.summary: The objective assessment and differential diagnosis of movement disorders, particularly Parkinson's disease (PD) and Essential Tremor (ET), remain challenging due to the subjectivity and limited temporal coverage of conventional in-clinic clinical assessments.Although consumer-grade smartphones equipped with inertial sensors provide a practical platform for continuous movement monitoring, existing deep-learning approaches remain constrained by their dependence on large, expertly annotated clinical datasets and their limited ability to learn generalized temporal representations.To address these challenges, this study proposes a self-supervised, patch-based Transformer framework that identifies clinically consistent candidate digital features from smartphone inertial timeseries data.The proposed framework employs a two-stage training strategy in which the Transformer encoder is first pre-trained using masked autoencoding on millions of unlabeled inertial sensor samples from the crowdsourced mPower dataset to learn robust latent representations of human movement.The pre-trained encoder is subsequently fine-tuned using a subject-wise protocol on the Mobile Device Tremor Dataset for multi-class tremor classification.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a multi-class classification accuracy of 95.85% and a macro F1-score of 95.52%, consistently outper

papers.title: The active self in autism: multisensory and sensorimotor foundations of bodily self-representation
papers.summary: Abstract The active self, understood as the embodied sense of self arising from goal-directed action and interaction with the environment, is supported by sensorimotor processes including multisensory integration and proprioception. Atypical self-representation in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been proposed to relate to differences in these processes. To clarify this relationship, we conducted a systematic conceptual review of 37 empirical studies published between 2010 and August 2025 examining multisensory and bodily components of the active self in ASD. The literature was synthesized across three themes: (1) multisensory integration, (2) self-bias and self-other differentiation, and (3) motor underpinnings of bodily awareness. Across studies, autistic participants frequently showed differences in multisensory timing and weighting, including reduced or delayed susceptibility to some bodily ownership illusions and greater reliance on proprioceptive or immediate sensory information. Evidence also indicated differences in the flexibility of peri- and interpersonal space, self-other differentiation, agency-related processing, and motor planning and execution. However, findings were not uniform across paradigms, developmental stages, or participant groups, with relatively preserved performance reported under some unimodal or low-noise conditions. papers.title: Executive Sensemaking of Generative AI Adoption at Enterprise Scale: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cross-Industry Executive Perspectives
papers.summary: This qualitative study examines how senior executives from technology, financial services, and consumer goods publicly make sense of enterprise-scale generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) adoption. Using a purposively selected, bounded single-case design, it applies reflexive thematic analysis to the complete transcript of one moderated industry panel. Three research questions ask: (1) how leaders describe adoption trajectories, maturity, and organizational arrangements; (2) how they reconcile regulation with creative, operational, and governance innovation; and (3) how they frame workforce roles, emerging competencies, and human oversight. Technology–organization–environment, diffusion-of-innovation, and organizational sensemaking perspectives inform interpretation. Nine themes were developed: production-grade diffusion; regulation as creative discipline; industrialized versus distinctive content; personalization and data trust; practitioner-led implementation; divergent workforce responses; critical-thinking demands; human-in-the-loop brand safety; and a shift toward generative engine optimization. Timestamped excerpts and explicit code-to-theme and theme-to-question mappings substantiate the analysis. These findings describe public executive narratives, not independently verified organizational outcomes. A single public transcript and single-analyst interpretation limit

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
papers.summary: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution. papers.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
papers.summary: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. papers.title: Adaptive Code Generation for Controlling Robots
papers.summary: Abstract Deploying robots as Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) in unknown and dynamic environments necessitates a transition from rigid command libraries toward intention-based autonomy, as natural language represents the only medium capable of articulating complex goals beyond the capacity of finite instruction sets. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a path toward natural language goal description, their integration introduces significant challenges: the formalization gap between imprecise intentions and executable actions, the taxonomy gap induced by unpredictable environments, and the challenge of maintaining temporal state and progress awareness. This work introduces an architectural framework that enables robotic control by leveraging generative AI. The system follows a dual-AI design: an LLM translates high-level intentions into executable program code restricted to a formal robotic library and constrained by verifiable syntax, while a Vision-Language Model (VLM) provides semantic grounding via a distillation process. To ensure robustness, the framework incorporates environment-driven replanning triggers based on geometric and semantic thresholds, complemented by continuous runtime monitoring and an adaptive planning loop. papers.title: Examining the mediating role of knowledge management processes between information literacy self-efficacy and user satisfaction with information systems
papers.summary: Introduction. This study examines the impact of information literacy self-efficacy on shaping knowledge management processes and user satisfaction with information systems among agricultural knowledge workers in Punjab, Pakistan. Although information literacy and knowledge management have been widely examined, limited research has modelled them as multidimensional higher-order constructs within agricultural research organisations. Method. Data were collected from 415 agricultural knowledge workers using stratified proportionate sampling: a survey instrument measured information literacy self-efficacy, knowledge management processes, and user satisfaction with information systems. Analysis. The data were analysed using SmartPLS 4. A disjoint two-stage approach was employed to estimate higher-order measurement and structural models. Reliability and validity of both lower- and higher-order constructs were assessed before hypothesis testing. Results. The results indicated that information literacy self-efficacy had a significant positive effect on knowledge management processes and user satisfaction with information systems.
